doc.title: Flip Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996

title: Playing with old friends at the Sarasota festival
summary: Phillips enjoyed seeing old friends at the festival and says he has had a great life.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. My name is Monk Rowe and it’s a great pleasure to have with us saxophonist Flip Phillips. And I have to ask you what it’s like to play with all these friends at this festival and it’s interesting to stand back stage and watch everybody come in and greet their friends.
Are you talking about Wednesday night? Yeah. That was quite a thrill for me because I haven’t seen some of these fellows in years. And I think it was the oldest band I ever played with.
There is a lot of years on stage.
Oh, yeah. And it was great to see everybody you know, and literally to see them. Because a lot of them aren’t here now, and it was great. I really enjoyed it you know.
Well you’ve had quite a career as a musician, would you do it all over again?
Oh, yeah. I had a great life, a wonderful life. It’s hard times, good times, but all-in-all everything was great.
